Bank loan: You can borrow up to 75% of the flat purchase price if the loan period is 25 years and below
HDB housing loan: You can borrow up to 75% of the flat purchase price However, you will be required to use all of your Ordinary Account savings above $20,000 first

column1: Downpayment and payment during key collection
Bank loan: The minimum downpayment and payment during key collection required is 25% of the purchase price You may use your Ordinary Account savings for your downpayment However, 5% of it has to be paid for in cash
HDB housing loan: The minimum downpayment and payment during key collection required is 20% of the purchase price which can be fully paid for using your Ordinary Account savings

column1: Use of CPF savings and previous property sales proceeds
Bank loan: You may use or retain any amount in your Ordinary Account (up to applicable limits)
HDB housing loan: If you are taking a second HDB loan(up to applicable limits), you and the essential occupier need to use 50% of the cash proceeds from the disposal of the existing or last-owned HDB flat

Bank loan: Bank interest rates fluctuate as these are more affected by the economic environment
HDB housing loan: The HDB interest rate is 0.1% above the Ordinary Account interest rate, which is currently 2.6%

Bank loan: Fluctuates depending on loan interest rate
HDB housing loan: Relatively constant due to stable interest rate

Bank loan: Early and late repayment penalties may apply Penalties are subject to the terms and conditions of the loan provider May only refinance loan with banks and unable to refinance to HDB loan
HDB housing loan: There is no early repayment penalty, but a late payment charge of 7.5% per annum Option to refinance to bank loan
